implementation_notes: The BCL provides the deferral: expose the real subject through a Lazy<T> (or Lazy<T>(Func<T>)) and read Value in the forwarding member, which creates the subject on first access. LazyThreadSafetyMode selects the policy - ExecutionAndPublication (the default: one thread builds, the others block, and exceptions from the factory are cached and rethrown), PublicationOnly (threads race, losers are discarded, exceptions are never cached) and None (no synchronization) - and the docs warn that a thread-safe Lazy<T> does not make the created object thread-safe. The classic hand-written stand-in is still justified when the proxy must implement a multi-method interface, forward identity members, or swap the subject at runtime; EF Core's lazy-loading proxies are the framework-provided version of that.
pitfalls: On the default mode the factory exception is cached and rethrown on every later access; transient failures must be retried inside the factory, and PublicationOnly is the way to avoid failure caching entirely.
The lazily created object itself is not made thread-safe by Lazy<T>; if several threads can reach the subject, its own members need synchronization.
A Lazy<T> that captures per-request state (a DbContext, a scope, an HttpClient) keeps it alive for the life of the proxy and can be evaluated after it was disposed.
